scope: independent receipt and source review of one artificially arranged synthetic Job
checks: Committed source and preregistration bytes, start marker and result identities match; old expired evidence and previous failed panel identities remain consistent.
Frozen source enforces the project Windows venv and three 4 GiB preflight checks before one owned Job; the process naturally exits after artificially arranged waiting.
Receipts report one complete and two discarded RSS samples, one retry and one verified empty exit; sampling arithmetic is consistent.
Job was assigned and resumed; the receipts report zero exit, launcher reaped, Job members zero and no cleanup error; sampled peaks remained within registered thresholds.
The registered synthetic workload contains no game, model, training data or network operation.
limitations: Evidence is based on worker and supervisor receipts and frozen code, not independent process or resource monitoring.
Maximum sampled member count of one does not prove the venv launcher and real Python child were both observed.
Individual preflight memory values were not retained; up to five seconds of artificial waiting pauses sampling and does not establish a hard memory bound.
This controlled artificial timing exercise does not prove the original failed panel had the same cause or change its failure.
Identity checks cannot exclude transient replacement followed by restoration; no process was rerun for this review.
